paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: This donut chart illustrates the distribution of samples as percentages across two dimensions: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer)”, is divided into four segments with varying shades of blue, representing standard deviations of 0.0 (darkest blue, 49.0%), 0.47 (medium-dark blue, 47.7%), 0.82 (medium blue, 5.0%), and 0.94 (lightest blue, 7.0%). The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)”, is divided into three segments with lighter shades of blue, representing maximum ambiguity values of 1 (lightest blue, 38.0%), 2 (medium-light blue, 39.0%), and 3 (medium blue, 14.2%). The chart includes two legends: one for the outer ring’s standard deviation categories and one for the inner ring’s maximum ambiguity categories. Each segment is labeled with its corresponding percentage value, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with the outer ring’s largest segment (Std: 0.0, 49.0%) positioned at the top left.
